blocking.issue: The required NOSCRIPT scenario contradicts foundation pack section 8.7 rule 1 and principle P3. It requires a second blocking State Store round trip for one Policy on one request: EVALSHA, then EVAL again after NOSCRIPT. Traffic management and resilience, the owner of the GCRA call, rules this out explicitly. There, NOSCRIPT applies `failureMode` and schedules a reload. An integration test written from this line would fail a conforming implementation and accept one that breaks the pack.
blocking.evidence: Line 142: "- `EVALSHA`, the cached form of pack section 8.8's single GCRA `EVAL`, meets `NOSCRIPT` after a script cache flush and resends `EVAL` within the same deadline." Foundation pack 8.7 rule 1: "Before the response is committed, each Policy makes at most one blocking State Store round trip per request." docs/architecture/09-traffic-management-and-resilience.md line 216: "Nodes `SCRIPT LOAD` every script at connect, reconnect and failover; `NOSCRIPT` applies `failureMode` and schedules a reload, so no request makes a second round trip (pack 8.7 rule 1)."
blocking.fix: Replace line 142 with: "- After a script cache flush, `EVALSHA` (the cached form of pack section 8.8's single GCRA `EVAL`) meets `NOSCRIPT`. That request applies the Policy's `failureMode` without a second round trip (pack section 8.7 rule 1). The Node reloads the script off the request path, and the next request's `EVALSHA` succeeds ([Traffic management and resilience](../architecture/09-traffic-management-and-resilience.md))." Mirror this in the Redis Cluster row if it asserts retries.
